checks_performed: Read only the authorized source-input JSON and revision-draft JSON.
Compared the exact universal target against the draft’s actual unconditional and conditional coverage.
Reconstructed every proof independently, including n=0, q=0, q=n, exact-size witnesses, integral radius R=floor(n/c), and constructive edge-edit transfers.

Wrote and ran an integer/Fraction-only exhaustive checker over all 1,100 labeled graphs with at most five vertices. It checked 186,356 constructive transfers, 427,797 gap/threshold cases, 1,041,196 approximation candidates, and 32,767 sparse certificates.
The same checker exhaustively tested 558 isolate-free maximum-degree-three Vertex Cover instances and converted 362,528 dominating sets through the degree-six gadget. All assertions passed.
Audited the PTAS and P-versus-NP implications separately from the finite checks.

claims.claim: For 0≤q≤n, a graph has a dominating set of exactly q vertices if and only if its domination number γ is at most q.
claims.evidence: An exact-q dominating set immediately gives γ≤q. Conversely, a minimum dominating set can be enlarged to q vertices because q≤n, and every superset of a dominating set remains dominating. This also covers n=q=0, where the empty set dominates the empty graph.
claims.search_method: Direct proof and exhaustive enumeration of every graph on at most five vertices and every q.

claims.claim: Greedy closed-neighborhood coverage has residual r≤n(1-1/q)^q whenever γ(G)≤q, for q≥1.
claims.evidence: Let U be the current residual and D an exact q-vertex dominating set. The q sets N[d]∩U cover U, so some has size at least |U|/q. Already selected vertices have zero intersection with U, hence greedy can realize at least this gain with an unselected vertex. Thus |U_i|≤(1-1/q)|U_{i-1}|, and iteration gives the claimed bound, including q=1.
claims.search_method: Averaging proof plus exhaustive integer verification of r q^q≤n(q-1)^q.

claims.claim: For arbitrary fixed c, greedy gives an exact polynomial-time triage: it solves the instance whenever r≤n/c or r>n(1-1/q)^q.
claims.evidence: For r≤n/c, each residual vertex is outside the greedy q-set S and has no edge to S. Adding one missing edge from a fixed s∈S to each residual vertex therefore uses exactly r edits and makes S dominating. If r exceeds the bound, Claim 1's contrapositive proves γ(G)>q, so (G,nil) is correct. The latter comparison is exactly r q^q>n(q-1)^q; radius comparisons use the source's computable-radius convention.
claims.search_method: Constructive proof and exhaustive testing of both branches using integer arithmetic.

claims.claim: Sidestep(Dominating Set,dist_e,n/c) is in FP for every fixed c≤e.
claims.evidence: For q≥1, ln(1-1/q)≤-1/q implies n(1-1/q)^q≤n/e≤n/c. Thus a residual either violates the theoretical bound, giving a correct nil answer on G, or can be repaired within n/c edits. For q=0, nil is correct whenever n>0, while the empty set is correct for n=0. All operations and the power comparison are polynomial-time.
claims.search_method: Analytic inequality, exact branch proof, and exhaustive validation of the underlying greedy constructions.

claims.claim: For every c, all instances with q≥1 and n-q≤n/c have a direct polynomial-time YES output.
claims.evidence: Choose any q-set S and s∈S. Only vertices outside S can be undominated. Adding su for each such undominated u uses at most n-q absent edges and makes S an exact-q dominating set of the edited graph.
claims.search_method: Direct construction and exhaustive testing for every graph and q through five vertices.

claims.claim: For every c, a computable sparse NO certificate is available when q+1 vertices have at most n/c incident edges in total.
claims.evidence: For an identified set T of q+1 such vertices, scan and delete the distinct edges incident with T. The edit count is at most n/c, every vertex of T becomes isolated, and hence every dominating set contains all q+1 vertices, ruling out an exact q-set. The construction and certificate verification are polynomial-time; choosing the q+1 lowest-degree vertices gives the stated efficiently detectable sufficient case.
claims.search_method: Direct certificate proof and exhaustive checking of all 32,767 candidate vertex subsets through five vertices.

claims.claim: Domination number is one-Lipschitz per edge edit, with a constructive transfer.
claims.evidence: If S dominates H, each vertex u not dominated by S in G is outside S and is dominated in H through a distinct edge su∈E(H)\E(G). Adding all such u to S yields a dominating set of G and adds at most |E(H)\E(G)| vertices. Applying the argument in both directions gives |γ(G)-γ(H)|≤|E(G)△E(H)|.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional constructive proof and 186,356 exhaustive transfer checks.

claims.claim: A radius-R sidestep solver decides every additive-gap instance whose YES case has γ(G)≤q-R and whose NO case has γ(G)>q+R.
claims.evidence: For every H at distance at most R, Lipschitzness gives γ(H)≤γ(G)+R≤q in the YES case and γ(H)≥γ(G)-R>q in the NO case. By Claim 0, every possible solver output is consequently a set in the first case and nil in the second, so its output type decides the promise.
claims.search_method: Lipschitz proof and exhaustive radius-0, radius-1, and radius-2 ball checks.

claims.claim: Any FP solver at fixed c yields a polynomial-time additive-2⌊n/c⌋ approximation for Minimum Dominating Set.
claims.evidence: Let R=⌊n/c⌋ and query every q. A set must be returned by q0=min(n,γ(G)+R): if q0<n this follows from γ(H)≤γ(G)+R, and q0=n is always feasible. Hence the first YES threshold q* satisfies q*≤γ(G)+R. Constructively transferring its q*-set back to G adds at most R vertices, giving size at most γ(G)+2R. There are only n+1 solver calls.
claims.search_method: Direct minimization-and-transfer proof plus exhaustive testing of all possible nearby returned graphs and witnesses through five vertices.

claims.claim: On graphs of maximum degree Δ, the preceding algorithm is a (1+2(Δ+1)/c)-approximation.
claims.evidence: For n>0, q dominators cover at most q(Δ+1) vertices, so γ(G)≥n/(Δ+1). Therefore γ+2⌊n/c⌋≤γ+2n/c≤(1+2(Δ+1)/c)γ. The empty graph is handled directly with optimum and output both zero.
claims.search_method: Closed-neighborhood counting proof and exact Fraction-based checks over the exhaustive graph set.

claims.claim: There is an exact approximation-preserving reduction from isolate-free Vertex Cover of maximum degree three to Dominating Set of maximum degree six.
claims.evidence: In the stated gadget, a vertex cover dominates every edge-vertex and, using isolate-freeness and retained original edges, every unchosen original vertex. Conversely, if a dominating set contains x_e, replace it by an endpoint of e. Every edge e is then covered because x_e was originally dominated only by itself or an endpoint. Size never increases, so γ equals τ. Original degree d becomes 2d≤6 and edge-vertices have degree two.
claims.search_method: Two-way exact reduction proof and exhaustive verification on 558 isolate-free maximum-degree-three instances, including all 362,528 dominating-set conversions.

claims.claim: The universal target implies a PTAS family for cubic Minimum Vertex Cover.
claims.evidence: For fixed ε>0, invoke the universal hypothesis at c=14/ε. Claims 8–9 give a (1+ε)-approximate dominating set on the degree-six gadget. Claim 10 converts it to a no-larger cover while preserving optimum. The composed running time is polynomial for every fixed ε; isolates can be discarded if cubic is interpreted as maximum degree three rather than 3-regular.
claims.search_method: Composition of the additive approximation, degree bound, and exact gadget; finite gadget components were exhaustively checked.

claims.claim: Conditional on the standard APX-hardness theorem for cubic Vertex Cover, the universal target holds if and only if P=NP.
claims.evidence: Let η>0 be the constant furnished by the stated APX-hardness theorem. The universal target supplies a solver at any fixed c>14/η, and Claims 8–11 then give a forbidden polynomial-time approximation unless P=NP. Conversely, if P=NP, self-reduction constructs an exact q-dominating set when one exists; extending a smaller set to size q and taking H=G gives a zero-edit sidestep solution for every c.
claims.search_method: Direct analysis of both complexity implications under the expressly stated APX-hardness premise.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an unconditional resolution for every fixed c>0. The draft rigorously proves the target for c≤e, gives correct polynomial-time YES/NO triage for additional arbitrary-c instances, and establishes—conditional on the stated standard APX-hardness theorem—that the universal assertion is equivalent to P=NP. It does not supply an unconditional solver or unconditional impossibility result for all c>e, so it does not fully resolve the target. These are nevertheless material and correct advances, giving VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. The draft labels its claimed_resolution as PARTIAL and its final writeup expressly disclaims an unconditional all-c resolution; that claimed resolution is therefore ACCURATE.
